intro.heading: The matchup
intro.body:
One game left, and this one is about the finish. **Klein Cain (5-4, 3-4)** closes the regular season at **Klein Forest (1-8, 1-6)** on Friday, November 6 at 7:00 PM at Klein Memorial Stadium. Thursday's loss to Magnolia ended Cain's playoff chase, so the finale carries a simpler stake: beat the Golden Eagles, finish **6-4**, and send the seniors out with a winning season.

The math closed Thursday night. Cain sits **sixth** in **District 15-6A**, and only the **top four** advance to the playoffs. Magnolia (5-2) and Klein were already beyond Cain's best possible district finish of **4-4** on Thursday, and Friday night's games filled in the rest of the picture. **Klein (7-1)** routed Klein Collins **71-21** and locked up **first place**. **Klein Oak (5-2)** shut out Magnolia West **55-0**, and **Tomball (5-2)** beat Tomball Memorial **47-26**, so Oak and Tomball joined Magnolia in a **three-way tie for second**. By Saturday, the rest of the picture had settled. Magnolia and Tomball have both **clinched** playoff spots, and Klein cannot be caught at the top, so **one spot** was left going into Thursday. **Klein Collins** took it, winning **56-28** at Klein Oak on Thursday night to claim the **fourth and final** berth. Collins finishes **5-3** in district and **6-4** overall, and Klein Oak ends at **5-3** in district and **5-5** overall. Magnolia hosts Tomball on Friday with the higher Division II seed on the line. None of it changes Cain's week. The finale is the Hurricanes' game alone.

Klein Forest comes in off its bye week on a **five-game losing streak**. Its last outing was a **48-20** loss at Magnolia on October 23, and its lone win was a **43-42** shootout over Magnolia West on September 17. Running back **Dejaune Etheridge** is the offense either way: he ran for **200 yards and three touchdowns** in the win over Magnolia West and scored all three Forest touchdowns against Magnolia. The Golden Eagles have given up **407 points in nine games**, but a team playing its finale at home with nothing to lose is never a formality.

Cain averages **35.9 points a game** and has played its best football in bursts this season. Neither team appeared in the **November 2** Class 6A state poll from Dave Campbell's Texas Football. For Cain's seniors, Friday is the last game of their high school careers, and a win still sends them out the right way: **6-4**, a winning season, and a victory in the finale. *One more Friday night. Finish it right.*

players.name: Eyan Johnson
players.copy: **Eyan Johnson (#16)** closes his Cain career as the engine of the offense: a team-high **79.7** rushing yards per game and **13** total touchdowns, 12 of them on the ground. Klein Forest has allowed **407** points in nine games, and Johnson is the back most likely to add to that total early.

players.name: Jace Hanks
players.copy: **Jace Hanks (#9)** has thrown **13** touchdown passes this season with a **104.6** quarterback rating, including two scores against Magnolia last week. He is also Cain's second-leading rusher at **71.0** yards per game, so Forest has to defend his legs as much as his arm in his final start of the season.

players.name: Israel Smith
players.copy: **Israel Smith (#8)** turned a slant into a **55-yard** touchdown against Magnolia, the score that put Cain in front in the third quarter. The sophomore is tied for the team lead with **3** receiving touchdowns and has a chance to add a fourth on Friday.

players.name: Easton Mizell
players.copy: **Easton Mizell (#47)** leads Cain with **3** interceptions, and the finale sets up his kind of game: a run-first opponent that has thrown one touchdown pass all season. If Forest is forced to throw while chasing the game, Mizell is the Hurricane most likely to be waiting on it.

players.name: Gage Hansberger
players.copy: **Gage Hansberger (#34)** leads Cain at **7.1** tackles per game, and his finale assignment is the simplest one on the scouting report: wherever **Dejaune Etheridge (#0)** goes, Hansberger has to get there first. The senior linebacker draws Forest's best player all night.

players.name: Dejaune Etheridge
players.copy: **Dejaune Etheridge (#0)** is the Klein Forest offense. The senior leads the Golden Eagles at **65.0** rushing yards per game with **8** rushing touchdowns, ran for **200** yards and three scores in their only win, and scored all three Forest touchdowns at Magnolia on October 23. If Cain can slow him down, Forest will need to find another way to move the ball, something it has struggled to do this season.

players.name: Jaylon Williams
players.copy: **Jaylon Williams (#4)** gives Forest a second runner at quarterback: **41.2** rushing yards per game and **4** rushing touchdowns, completing **58.0** percent of his passes when he does throw. Cain's edge discipline gets tested every time he keeps the ball.

players.name: Ryan Langford-Mathis
players.copy: **Ryan Langford-Mathis (#18)** is Forest's one proven downfield threat at **69.0** receiving yards per game, more than triple the Golden Eagles' next receiver. When Forest throws, it is usually looking for him, and Cain's secondary can shade his way.

players.name: Aadeyn Brown
players.copy: **Aadeyn Brown (#22)** spells Etheridge in the backfield at **20.7** rushing yards per game. Forest leans on its ground game because the passing attack has produced just **one** touchdown all season, so Brown's carries matter more than the total suggests.

recruiting.heading: Klein Forest recruiting notes
recruiting.note: The finale brings the quietest recruiting board of the season. A roster-wide check of On3, 247Sports and Rivals indexed coverage on November 2 found no Klein Forest player with a verified commitment, offer list or recruiting ranking, and the Golden Eagles' best player is no exception. Cain's one rated recruit remains its junior back, whose offer list was verified in late October.

rows.name: Dejaune Etheridge
rows.note: Forest's senior workhorse (65.0 rushing yards per game, 8 rushing touchdowns, a 200-yard and three-touchdown game against Magnolia West) has no recruiting profile, offer list or commitment in On3, 247Sports or Rivals indexed coverage as of November 2. Production has not translated into recruiting attention yet.

rows.name: Ryan Langford-Mathis
rows.note: Forest's leading receiver at 69.0 yards per game likewise has no verified recruiting profile or offers in indexed On3, 247Sports or Rivals coverage as of November 2.

rows.name: Earl Oguinn Jr.
rows.note: Cain's junior back is a three-star recruit in the class of 2028 (On3 industry rating 83.67, the No. 49 running back in the class). As verified October 25, On3 lists offers from SMU, LSU, Iowa State, Missouri State and UTSA.

items.title: Win the Etheridge matchup
items.body: Everything Forest does runs through **Dejaune Etheridge (#0)**, who has scored **8** of the Golden Eagles' rushing touchdowns and all three of their scores at Magnolia. Cain's front has to set the edge, gang-tackle him and make someone else beat them. If Etheridge is held near his **65.0** yards per game or below, Forest's offense stalls.

items.title: Start fast and make Forest chase
items.body: Forest has scored **120** points in nine games, **13.3** a night, and its passing game has produced **one** touchdown. An early two-score lead forces the Golden Eagles out of the only thing they do well. Cain has started slowly in its losses; the finale is the night to flip that script in the first quarter.

items.title: No freebies for a team with nothing to lose
items.body: A 1-8 team playing its finale at home will empty the playbook: fakes, onside kicks, fourth-down gambles. Cain cannot hand that kind of team short fields or cheap points. Clean special teams, no turnovers in its own end, and make Forest drive the length of the field for everything it gets.

items.title: Finish drives, finish the season
items.body: Cain averages **35.9** points a game but settled too often in the losses that ended the playoff chase. Friday is about the seniors: turn red-zone trips into touchdowns, close out a **6-4** finish, and send the class of 2027 out with a winning season and a win in its last game together.

final.headline: Klein Cain rolls past Klein Forest 66-24 to close the season 6-4
final.byline: Cain Game Day desk · Updated 10:14 PM CT
final.body:
Klein Cain closed the 2026 season with a **66-24 win** over Klein Forest on Friday night at Klein Memorial Stadium. The Hurricanes led **38-10 at halftime**, scored in every quarter, and finished **6-4 overall and 4-4 in District 15-6A**. The Hurricanes missed the playoffs, but finished with a winning record, and Friday's finale was never in doubt after the first quarter.

Cain wasted no time. A double reverse to **Israel Smith (#8)** went **60 yards** down the right sideline to the Forest 15, and after a Forest penalty, **Jace Hanks (#9)** put the ball in the right corner of the end zone, where Smith went up and got it. **7-0 with 11:44 left in the first quarter.**

Forest's first drive ran into **Christian Lovell (#45)**. Lovell dropped the quarterback for a **tackle for loss** on a keeper, then came back with a third-down sack to force the punt. Cain's defense was making plays early.

Hanks struck again on the next series, finding **Tyson Freeman (#17)** for a **54-yard touchdown pass**. The offensive line gave him all day to throw. **14-0 with 7:44 left in the first.**

Forest's next possession ended on a heave down the left sideline that **Reggie Yarbough (#15)** picked off at the Cain 35. Cain drove it from there: **Eyan Johnson (#16)** carried for 13, Freeman caught one on the right sideline, Johnson pushed it to the 4, and two plays later Johnson ran it in up the middle. **21-0 with 2:29 left in the first quarter.**

Forest got on the board behind **Dejaune Etheridge (#0)**. Etheridge turned a slant into a **48-yard catch and run**, then took a direct snap on fourth-and-2 at the start of the second quarter and scored off the left side. **21-7 at 11:55.**

Cain answered on a drive that included a pair of ejections. Offsetting unsportsmanlike conduct penalties on the second play got Smith and a Forest player ejected from the game. Two plays later Hanks threw a screen to **Earl Oguinn Jr. (#1)**, who turned up the left sideline and outran everyone for the touchdown. **28-7 with 10:46 left in the half.**

Another interception set up Cain's next score. **AJ Carroll (#11)** intercepted a deep ball down the left sideline at 9:40, **Preston Kretch (#48)** ran through tacklers on a catch to move Cain inside the 10, and Hanks found **Braylon Francis (#20)** on the right side for the score. **35-7 with 8:00 left**, and Hanks had thrown touchdown passes to **four different receivers** in the half.

Forest drove to the Cain 3 after a deep catch by Etheridge that also drew a pass interference flag. But Cain's defense held, with **Gage Hansberger (#34)** making the stop on third down. Forest settled for a field goal at 3:37. **35-10.**

Senior quarterback **Trey Reyes (#5)** got his chance on Cain's final drive of the half. After **Dillion Dotson (#80)** returned the kickoff to the Forest 38, Reyes took over for the series in his final game. Two holding calls pushed Cain back to second-and-30, catches by **Deaunte Barr (#18)** and a roughing-the-passer flag kept the drive alive, an Oguinn touchdown came back on a block in the back, and **Sage DesAutels (#4)** finished it with a field goal. **38-10 at halftime.**

Forest opened the second half with a scoring drive, finished by **Aadeyn Brown (#22)** from 15 yards out at 7:44 of the third. **38-17.**

Reyes took over from there and led Cain right back down the field. He kept for 15, flipped a pass to Barr while being sacked for a first down, and finished the drive with an **11-yard touchdown pass to Barr** at 5:39. **45-17.**

The next two Forest possessions ended in interceptions. **Christian Redeo (#7)** returned the first one for a **pick-six** to make it 52-17. **Daniel Rogers (#25)** intercepted Forest on its next series. Oguinn cashed that one in himself, a 16-yard run to the 3 and then the touchdown run at 1:36. **59-17.**

Cain added one more touchdown in the fourth quarter, but it came after a penalty wiped out a long scoring pass. A long Reyes touchdown pass to Kretch was called back for an ineligible receiver downfield, so Cain ran it in instead, Johnson scoring from the 3 for his **second touchdown** of the night. **66-17.** Etheridge answered with an **18-yard touchdown run** up the middle for Forest, Reyes took the final snaps and the kneel-downs, and that was the season. **Final: Klein Cain 66, Klein Forest 24.**

Cain finishes **6-4**, short of the playoffs but with a winning record. Friday gave the Hurricanes a chance to send their seniors out with a win, and they did it in convincing fashion.

notes.heading: Five touchdown passes, five receivers
paragraphs: Hanks threw four touchdown passes in the first half, one each to Smith, Freeman, Oguinn Jr. and Francis. Reyes added the fifth in the third quarter, to Barr. Five Cain touchdown passes on the night went to five different receivers.

notes.heading: Four interceptions
paragraphs: The Cain defense picked off four passes: Yarbough in the first quarter, Carroll in the second, Redeo (returned for a touchdown) and Rogers in the third. Lovell also had a tackle for loss and a sack on Forest's opening drive. Cain's defense was making its presence felt from the start.

notes.heading: A senior's finish
paragraphs: After backing up Hanks all season, senior **Trey Reyes (#5)** got a series in the second quarter and then ran the offense for most of the second half in his final game.

He threw a touchdown pass and had two more scores wiped out by penalties on his drives: an Oguinn touchdown on a block in the back in the second quarter, and a long pass to Kretch on an ineligible receiver penalty in the fourth. Reyes also took the final kneel-downs.
